# ADR-0016: A development gateway with explicit production boundary

Recorded: 11 October 2026. Retrospective project decision; not a bank governance approval.

## Status

Accepted; local HTTP gateway implemented

## Context

The lab should have one entry point for UI, design pages and business/control APIs.

## Decision

Use an Nginx gateway bound to host loopback, serving the lab portal and proxying /api/ to the single harness. Regional authenticated business gateways remain a target deployment design.

## Alternatives

Expose SQL/OPA directly to the user; describe distributed gateways as already implemented.

## Consequences

Local HTTP and insecure SQL are synthetic-lab conveniences. Access from a remote workstation should use an SSH tunnel; bank use requires approved TLS, identity, authorization and regional ingress. Public assets and live-mode JSON must be readable by Nginx workers, and .mjs must use a JavaScript MIME type. Local health requests bypass host proxy settings. Upstream API and Grafana addresses are refreshed through Docker DNS, rather than retained for the gateway lifetime, so container image replacements do not require an operator to restart the gateway.

## Evidence

infra/nginx.conf; infra/Gateway.Dockerfile; compose.yaml; poc/tests/gateway_dns_acceptance.py; docs/security/observability-upgrade-2026-10-16.json

## Gate

Gateway readiness and API routes work; only the gateway port is published; remote deployment runbook distinguishes tunnel access from production exposure. Move the real Grafana container to a different Docker address and require recovery through the unchanged gateway process; restore its original network attachment afterwards.
